full_judgment: 23. In the instant writ petitions, we are dealing with constitutionality of a primary legislation. In case of primary legislation, there is a presumption in favour of constitutionality. This means, primary legislation as a whole or any provision(s) thereof will not be declared unconstitutional unless the writ petitioner can clearly show, beyond doubt, that the same is violative of Article 7 or Part III of the Constitution. It may happen that the argument advanced in favour of declaring a statutory provision unconstitutional is convincing but on a reasonable alternative interpretation, the provision can be concluded to be constitutional; in such a case, it is a settled principle that the Court should apply the doctrine of "reading in" and adopt the interpretation that favours constitutionality.
